As a result, GetEqualityComparer on UntrustedData returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default. This has nothing to do with the generator/analyzer crash in MP-2283. Any dictionary or hash set built from untrusted payload keys loses its SipHash-based protection, so crafted keys could degrade those collections and be used for denial of service. This includes Location.None, which is what Diagnostic.Create produces when it is given a null location. Some location helpers return null even for code in the project being compiled. One example is the new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation: it only accepts PropertyDeclarationSyntax, so for a positional record parameter (ParameterSyntax) it returns null. The member loop already handles that case at line 926. So BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull for a source-declared positional record property used to throw InvalidCastException and is now silently dropped, with no diagnostic at all. Other diagnostics are dropped the same way whenever their location helper returns null for source code (for example PartialTypeRequired with a null primaryLocation). The filter should only drop locations that come from metadata or another compilation, not every missing location for a source symbol.
